diagnostics.summary: [redacted: Kernel message text, EUPL localisation resource]
diagnostics.fix: The condition has a token the DSL parser did not expect (a syntax slip the kernel reports with no message of its own). The most common causes, in order: (1) a BOOLEAN literal must be CAPITALIZED — write `True` / `False`, not the JSON `true` / `false` (e.g. `[Flag] == True`); (2) a string value must be DOUBLE-QUOTED — `[Status] == "OPEN"`; (3) operator/keyword names are case-sensitive PascalCase — `FieldFilled`, `And`, `Or`, `Not`; (4) a FIELD used as a comparison VALUE must be BRACKETED — `[Approved] != True`, not `Approved != True` (bare names belong only inside a function/predicate's parentheses, like `FieldFilled(Approved)`). Re-check the token at the reported position against these.
diagnostics.explain: MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN is the kernel's generic parse error — a token appeared where the grammar did not allow it — and it is raised WITHOUT a message, so the likely cause has to be inferred from the DSL's literal/keyword conventions (capitalized booleans True/False, double-quoted strings, case-sensitive PascalCase operators).
